words.enExample: A walk at noon recharges my focus.
words.zhExample: 中午走一圈，给专注力充电。
words.note: 💡 re-（再）+ charge。搭 recharge batteries。休息不是偷懒，是 recharge。

words.enExample: A mid-afternoon slump is normal; plan around it.
words.zhExample: 下午中段的萎靡很正常，绕着它安排。
words.note: 💡 搭 hit a slump。识别自己的 slump 时段，别硬扛。

words.enExample: Deep work builds mental stamina over time.
words.zhExample: 深度工作，随时间积累脑力耐力。
words.note: 💡 不可数。搭 build stamina。精力管理练的是 stamina，不是时长。

words.zhExample: 来一段 25 分钟冲刺，然后休息。
words.note: 💡 搭 a sprint。和 slump 相对：sprint 之后必须 rest。

words.enExample: I decompress by cooking after work.
words.note: 💡 de-（去）+ compress（压）。搭 decompress from。休息也是工作的一部分=会 decompress。

essay.title: Rest Is Part of the Work
essay.author: 佚名
paragraphs: We treat rest as a reward we earn after the work is done, something to be squeezed into the margins of a busy life. But the truth is simpler and harder to accept: rest is not the opposite of work, it is part of the work. A mind that never stops is a tool left running until it wears down.

Think of attention as a battery. Every decision, every small reply, every task you half-finish drains it a little, whether or not you notice. By mid-afternoon most people are not lazy; they are simply running on empty.

The problem is not that we rest too little, but that we rest too poorly. Scrolling through a phone feels like a break and yet leaves the mind busier than before. Real rest has a texture: it is unhurried, it asks nothing of you, and it gives you back the quiet you started the day without.

I learned this the hard way, during a season when I boasted about never taking a day off. My output looked the same on the surface, but the ideas grew thin, and the small errors multiplied. The work did not stop; it simply got worse while I was still at the desk.

So build rest into the shape of the day the way you would build in a meeting. A walk with no purpose, a chapter of a book, ten minutes with nothing in your hands. The work will still be there when you return, and you will meet it with a fuller mind than the one that left.
translations: 我们把休息当作工作完成之后才配得到的奖赏，是塞进忙碌生活缝隙里的东西。但真相更简单，也更难接受：休息不是工作的对立面，它就是工作的一部分。一颗从不停歇的心，是把工具一直开着直到它磨损殆尽。
把注意力想成一块电池。每一个决定、每一条简短的回复、每一件你做到一半的事，都在悄悄消耗它，无论你是否察觉。到了下午中段，大多数人并不是懒，而只是彻底没电了。
问题不在于我们休息得太少，而在于休息得太糟。刷手机看似是种放松，却让脑子比之前更忙。真正的休息有一种质感：它从容不迫，不向你索取任何东西，并把它还给那份你清早出门时就已经丢失的安静。
我是吃了苦头才学到这一点的，那段时间我以从不休假为傲。我的产出表面上看没什么变化，但想法变得稀薄，小错误不断增多。工作并没有停下；它只是趁我还坐在桌前，悄悄变糟了。
所以，要把休息像安排会议那样，嵌进一天的轮廓里。一场漫无目的的散步，一章书，或者双手空空地待上十分钟。你回来时，工作仍在那里，而你迎接它的，会比离开时那颗心，更饱满一些。

grammar.point: 并列否定结构 not A but B
grammar.example: But the truth is simpler and harder to accept: rest is not the opposite of work, but part of the work.
grammar.note: not A but B 表示「不是 A，而是 B」，先用否定推开第一种说法，再用 but 把重心落在后者。句中把「对立面」换成「一部分」，彻底改写了休息的语义位置。 举一反三：同结构还有 not a break but a part of the plan、it is not weakness but wisdom。

grammar.example: Scrolling through a phone feels like a break and yet leaves the mind busier than before.
grammar.note: 现在分词 scrolling 引导的短语作主语，把「刷手机」这个行为整体化；feels 与 leaves 并列作谓语，busier than before 是比较级作宾语补足语，点出「看似放松、实则更累」的反差。 举一反三：同类主语如 reading widely opens the mind、sitting still restores the calm。

grammar.point: the way 引导方式状语从句（省略 as）
grammar.example: So build rest into the shape of the day the way you would build in a meeting.
grammar.note: the way 在此相当于 as / in the way that，引导方式状语从句说明「嵌入」的方式，口语中常省略连词。主句是祈使句 build...，语气直接而有力。 举一反三：也可写成 just as you would build in a meeting，或 as you schedule a meeting。

vocab.enExample: A short rest after lunch helped her focus.
vocab.zhExample: 午后的短暂休息让她重新集中了注意力。
vocab.note: 用法：指工作或活动之间的停顿，也可作动词

vocab.enExample: Please give this report your full attention.
vocab.zhExample: 请对这份报告投入你全部的注意力。
vocab.note: 用法：把心思集中在某事上的能力，常接 to

vocab.enExample: Making small decisions all day can be surprisingly tiring.
vocab.zhExample: 一整天做各种小决定，会累得超乎想象。
vocab.note: 用法：经过思考后作出的选择，动词为 decide

vocab.enExample: The long meeting drained what little energy he had left.
vocab.zhExample: 那场漫长的会议耗光了他所剩无几的精力。
vocab.note: 用法：慢慢抽走精力、金钱或液体，名词亦可用

vocab.enExample: She spoke in an unhurried voice that calmed everyone.
vocab.zhExample: 她用从容的语调说话，让所有人都平静下来。
vocab.note: 用法：形容节奏舒缓、没有紧迫感

vocab.enExample: Working without breaks will wear you down over time.
vocab.zhExample: 不休息地工作，久而久之会把你拖垮。
vocab.note: 用法：长期使用后变旧变坏，常见搭配 wear down / wear out

vocab.enExample: He used to boast about answering emails at midnight.
vocab.zhExample: 他过去常以半夜回邮件为傲。
vocab.note: 用法：自豪地谈论某事，语气可褒可贬

vocab.enExample: Leave a margin in your schedule for the unexpected.
vocab.zhExample: 在日程里为意外留出一点余地。
vocab.note: 用法：引申为时间或资源上留出的余量
